tagline: West on 290, past a president's porch and his cattle.
intro: US 290 leaves Johnson City, where the Johnson family moved in 1913 when the future president was five, and heads west through the Hill Country toward Fredericksburg. The highway is promoted these days as Wine Road 290, the wine trail to the wineries and vineyards around Fredericksburg, a town long known for its peaches.

Johnson left his ranch on the Pedernales to the public on condition that it remain a working ranch and not become a sterile relic of the past. Hereford cattle still roam it, as they have since he started his herd in 1957.

moments.title: Hye
moments.text: Johnson reportedly mailed his first letter at the Hye post office at the age of four, and in 1965 he came back to its porch to swear in a Postmaster General.

moments.title: LBJ Ranch
moments.text: A free permit from the state park visitor center near Stonewall opens the drive past the Texas White House, the family cemetery and one of the five presidential Jetstars.

moments.title: Fredericksburg
moments.text: German settlers founded the town in 1846 and named it for Prince Frederick of Prussia, and its first generations spoke a Texas German, refusing at first to learn English.
